meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (European continental codified law; French Civil Code, Code de commerce; prudential rule-making by the ACPR within the European Single Rulebook framework)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L.561-1 through L.561-57 and R.561-1 through R.561-27 of the Code monétaire et financier (CMF), as amended by Loi n°2024-364 du 22 avril 2024 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD); the French beneficial ownership (UBO) register established by Décret n°2017-1094 du 2 août 2017 and annexed to the RCS; ACPR General Regulation (Règlement n°2019-03) and ACPR Guidance on licensing and AML/CFT fit-and-proper; restrictions on public UBO access resulting from the CJEU judgment of 22 November 2022, Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20 (WM and Sovim) and Conseil d'État Decision n°475145 of 7 July 2023.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of each UBO and each appointed manager (gérant)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority in the holder's country of origin (e.g., French Ministère de l'Intérieur or equivalent foreign authority)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for member states of the 1961 Hague Convention; Consular Legalization for non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police certificate / criminal records extract (extrait de casier judiciaire or equivalent) for each UBO and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Casier Judiciaire National (French Ministry of Justice) or the equivalent criminal record authority in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, plus certified French translation by a court-approved translator (traducteur assermenté)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation / certificate of good standing (or equivalent registration extract) for any corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Register of Commerce in the corporate UBO's jurisdiction of establishment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, plus certified French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or proof of cash funds for the share capital contribution (attestation de dépôt des fonds)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The French credit institution or licensed depositary holding the SARL's share capital in escrow
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Private deed (sous seing privé) acceptable; no apostille required, but certified French translation of any foreign bank letter is mandatory

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all UBOs, shareholders, managers, and initial beneficiaries against: (i) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list (DG FISMA), (ii) United Nations Security Council sanctions and asset-freezing lists, (iii) OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists for any USD clearing or correspondent exposure, (iv) the French national asset-freezing regime under Décret n°2020-118 du 12 février 2020 and the ACPR list of 'gels internationaux', and (v) PEP status as defined under Article L.561-10 CMF. Enhanced due diligence is triggered by any PEP match, high-risk third-country nexus, or adverse media hit; screening must be repeated at least every 90 days and re-validated at the point of ACPR licence filing in accordance with ACPR position-recommendation publications and the European Supervisory Authorities' Risk Factor Guidelines.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.aml_cft_compliance_architecture_note: The SARL must establish a proportionate AML/CFT system prior to ACPR on-site validation: internal control manual (Article L.561-32 CMF), a CDD/UBO risk matrix, transaction monitoring procedures, mandatory STR (TRACFIN) reporting, and a duly designated AML/CFT compliance officer; failure to evidence this architecture at pre-incorporation stage is an automatic licence-refusal trigger criterion.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_piercing_commentary: For the target scope 'Virtual IBAN Issuance and Digital Wallet Reserve Management', Article L.561-2 CMF requires the RBE to disclose all legal persons holding more than 25% of the registered capital or voting rights, or exercising control via other means; full chain-of-title memory flow (each intermediate holding vehicle) must be documented; no nominee toleration is permitted for ACPR-licensed EMI structures.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.us_private_exchange_benchmark_reference: Private capital exchange listings in the United States accept French SARL UBO documentation with the same bundle, subject to US Beneficial Ownership Information (BOI) requirements under the Corporate Transparency Act; French UBO filings do not substitute, and separate LLC/S-LLC BOI reports under FinCEN are required.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.reporting_obligation_projection_warning: The registry authority in the country of final incorporation reserves the right to request supplemental source-of-funds evidence for any UBO whose declared net worth is inconsistent with the subscribed capital; such supplemental requests are tax-neutral but may postpone RCS issuance of the Kbis by up to 30 days.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.supporting_evidence_footnotes: Identification and verification evidence must be dated no earlier than 3 months prior to submission; translations must bear the seal of the court-approved translator and, when executed outside France, the apostille or consular legalization certificate.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI Guichet Unique (Formalités des entreprises) – official portal: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; name-search and RCS cross-reference databases: data.inpi.fr and infogreffe.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name and corporate object must be expressed in French characters in all statutory instruments and RCS filings; Loi n°94-665 du 4 août 1994 (Loi Toubon) mandates French-language mandatory content in deeds and public registers; a foreign denomination may appear as a concurrent trade name (nom commercial) but the legal RCS name must be presented in Latin-script French transliteration
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: ANTILLES / GUYANE / RÉUNION (or any territorial denom création implying official sponsorship)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No formal statutory name reservation exists in France; name clearance is obtained via an instantaneous search of the RCS (data.inpi.fr) and an optional INPI trademark pre-filing for the denomination. Upon administrative rejection by the Guichet Unique: (i) the applicant may file a written réclamation within 15 days through the INPI portal, providing the greffe with case-law evidence of non-confusing identity; (ii) if the refusal is grounded on conflict with an existing RCS name, the applicant may initiate an action for unfair competition (action en concurrence déloyale) before the Tribunal de commerce, or request the greffe's mediation (Article R.123-5 Code de commerce); (iii) in the absence of a twelve-day resolution, a summary application (référé) before the President of the Tribunal de commerce may suspend the conflicting registration; (iv) after all administrative remedies are exhausted, an appeal lies to the Cour d'appel in the jurisdiction where the Tribunal de commerce sits, with any final merits decision sealed by the Cour de cassation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.documentation_residual_risk: Name clearance does not annul trademark priority; a third-party trademark owner may still assert opposition under the Code de la propriété intellectuelle within 30 days of INPI publication (Article L.712-4), hence trademark search is included in the pre-incorporation budget.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.prohibited_tokens_approval_notes: Use of the token 'FRANCE' is permissible only in a manner that does not imply French State endorsement; specific approval from the Premier Ministre or the relevant Ministry is mandatory for identifiers invoking sovereignty, public order, or regulated financial status.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.notice_of_name_withdrawal: Upon rejection of the desired name, the applicant automatically holds a 10-business-day right to select a revised name without additional filing fee.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.record_keeping: The Registry Bureau maintains the final RCS denomination choice on record; any subsequent change requires a formal amendment to the articles of association and a new guichet unique declaration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.agency_recommendation: When proceeding with a preferred trade denomination, the SRO recommends filing the corresponding French semi-textual (semi-figurative) trademark application to the INPI within the 30-day reservation window to block opportunistic third-party filings.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not acceptable as the sole registered office for a licensed EMI; Article L.223-10 Code de commerce requires a genuine French siège social; commercial business-center domiciliation (Loi n°2011-284 du 3 mars 2011) is tolerated for clerical purposes only. For ACPR licensing under Article L.526-10 CMF, the SARL must demonstrate permanent physical presence in France: in-house compliance, AML officers, board-level decision capability, audit-trail maintenance, and personnel on site. A pure virtual office (mail-forwarding only) renders the licence application invalid ab initio.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (>85% in the first 24 months following ACPR licence issuance); ACPR conducts unannounced onsite missions under Article L.612-23 CMF, including thematic inspections of UBO records, AML/CFT software, and e-money reserve safeguarding accounts; targeted inspections may occur within 6 months of licence grant where the UBO structure involves non-EU shareholders. A separate 'contrôle permanent' visit is expected annually, and frequent 'sham office' inspection sweeps occur in quarters Q1 and Q3 with adverse action (Kbis suspension) for mismatched signage.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.effective_management_presence: The ACPR considers Article L.526-10 CMF as requiring at least one manager or compliance officer with crucifix residence in France. Remote-only CA/board meetings fail the EU EMIR/monetary regulator market practice test, and reserved management powers must be exercised in French physical meetings.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.relocation_materiality: The ACPR requires that the SARL's external management and commercial substance remain within France for the entire license period; delegation of key regulatory functions to non-French EU subcontractors is permissible only under ACPR approval and does not erode the requirement for a substantiated French HQ.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book I, Title II, Article L.123-1 et seq. (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés); Book II, Title III, Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL structure and management); Article L.223-7 (deposit of cash share capital); Article L.210-2 (lawful business purpose); complemented by French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Book V, Articles L.525-1, L.526-1 to L.526-8 and Article L.526-4 (mandatory EUR 350,000 initial capital for electronic money institutions).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), transmitting to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce in whose district the registered office is located (e.g., Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce de Paris) for final registration on the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Dossier de création d'entreprise (single telemetric file) comprising the Statuts (Articles of Association), the M0 / formalité de création declaration, legal publication certificate, bank's blocked-fund certificate, proof of office address and beneficial-owner declaration; the issued instrument is the Extrait K-bis.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital under Code de commerce Article L.223-2 for a SARL; however, under Code monétaire et financier Article L.526-4, the EMI must have a statutorily paid-up initial capital of at least EUR 350,000 entirely subscribed and deposited in a blocked escrow-style cash account opened with a credit institution or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; funds are irrevocably released only after RCS registration (K-bis) and ACPR licence conditions are met.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] SARL — adopted unanimously on [DATE] in Paris. 1. The share capital of EUR 350,000 is subscribed in full and paid into the blocked account of [Bank] under Code de commerce Article L.223-7, divided into 3,500 shares of EUR 100 each. 2. The registered office is fixed at [ADDRESS] within the jurisdiction of the Tribunal de Commerce de Paris; the legal announcement shall be published in the Journal d'Annonces Légales of Paris. 3. Mr./Ms. [NAME] is appointed Gérant for an indefinite term with all powers granted by law and the Statuts. 4. The Gérant is authorized to file the incorporation dossier at the Guichet Unique and to initiate ACPR licensing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Distinctiveness Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI national trade-mark database (data.inpi.fr) and Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés name database via Greffe/Infogreffe.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a negative distinctiveness search against identical, confusingly similar, or prior registered corporate names and French/EU trademarks covering financial services classes 35, 36, 38 and 42. Validate a denomination with French commercial-name grammar, then reserve the domain and order a single search report to evidence availability for the Greffe.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name conflict or confusing similarity is detected, immediately file a substitute name from the alternative list; no administrative appeal is available, but a reasoned rebuttal may be addressed to the Greffe if the conflicting mark is inactive or in a dissimilar class.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Statuts (SARL Articles of Association)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel / notary; final registration controller is the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft French-law Statuts covering corporate form (SARL), share classes and transfer restrictions, corporate-purpose clause limited to electronic money issuance and digital wallet management, Gérant powers and removal procedure, quorum/majority rules for collective decisions, financial-year closure, and audit appointment triggers. Every shareholder must sign the Statuts; in-kind contributions of real property require authenticity before a notary, and non-cash assets exceeding EUR 30,000 require a commissaire aux apports valuation report annexed to the Statuts.
required_dossiers: Commissaire aux apports report (if in-kind contribution)
Identity documents of shareholders and Gérant
Certificate of non-condemnation (pièce judiciaire) for the Gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe identifies a statutory defect, file a supplementary notarial or private rectification deed (acte rectificatif) executed by all shareholders within 15 days of the registry's observations; full re-execution is required only for materially invalid objects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocked Deposit of Cash Share Capital and Bank Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Bank of the company's choice or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations if no bank account can be opened.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the company being formed. Wire-transfer EUR 350,000 from each subscriber's account providing source-of-funds documentation under AML/CTF rules (Code monétaire et financier Article L.561-5). The depositary bank issues a certificate of deposit (attestation de blocage) under Article L.223-7 of the Code de commerce stating the exact amount, the subscriber names, and the release condition that funds become available only upon production of the K-bis.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the deposit on AML suspicion, supplement the file with audited bank statements, notarial provenance certificates, and tax-residence declarations; if no commercial bank cooperates, deposit the funds at Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations under the same blocking regime.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Legal Formation Notice in a Licensed Journal d'Annonces Légales
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal-announcement gazette (JAL) authorized by the Prefecture of the département of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a mandatory notice containing the corporate form (SARL), company name, share capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, the Gérants' names and birth dates, and the competent RCS court. Submit the text online, pay the gazette fee, and obtain the attestation de parution expressing the exact publication date and issue number.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney of the filer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or the attestation contains errors, request a priority reprint or a corrective notice; typographical errors in the name or capital must be republished to avoid Greffe rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: E-Filing of the Incorporation File at the Guichet Unique (INPI) and RCS Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique portal (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) operated by INPI; substantive review and registration by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Assemble the complete telemetric dossier: executed Statuts, M0 declaration, publication certificate, blocked-fund certificate, domiciliation agreement, Gérant identity and judicial records, and the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) declaration. Submit through the Guichet Unique, electronically sign, and pay the registry fees; the Greffe verifies legality and enters the company in the RCS, ultimately issuing the Extrait K-bis and the SIREN number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is returned with observations, cure all defects within 15 days via the Guichet Unique workspace; if the 15-day cure period is missed, the file is rejected and must be re-submitted with a new publication if the notice has expired.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of K-bis, SIREN/SIRET Numbers and Release of Blocked Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; INSEE; depositary bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration, retrieve the Extrait K-bis containing the SIREN, SIRET, APE/NAF code (mapped from ISIC 6619 to NAF 6492Z), and the RCS number. Provide the K-bis to the bank to trigger release of the EUR 350,000 into the company's operational account; register the company with URSSAF as an employer and apply for the security umbrella (code APE).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses release, issue a K-bis certified copy from the Greffe and a written release mandate from the Gérant; if the INSEE code is wrong, apply for INSEE code correction through the Guichet Unique.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: BODACC Publicity and Definitive Third-Party Validity
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Bulletin Officiel des Annonces Civiles et Commerciales (BODACC).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure automatic publication of the incorporation entry in the BODACC within 8 days of RCS registration; verify the entry for exact company name, capital, registered office and Gérant; challenge any incorrect entry by filing a written objection with the Greffe.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For erroneous or delayed BODACC publication, address a rectification request to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and, failing that, bring an incidental summary petition (référé) before the President of the commercial court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) — Banque de France, 4 Place de Budapest, 75009 Paris; for workplace, fire and environmental controls, the Direction Régionale de l'Économie, de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités (DREETS) of the registered office's region.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Agrément d'établissement de monnaie électronique (Electronic Money Institution authorization) under Articles L.525-1 and L.526-1 of the French Monetary and Financial Code, transposing Directive 2009/110/EC; the authorization permits issuing, distributing and redeeming e-money, operating payment accounts and executing SEPA credit transfers and Central-Bank clearing settlement through participation in Banque de France payment systems (TARGET2-SEPI).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique — Direction Générale de la Prévention des Risques (DGPR), with local enforcement by the Préfecture and DREETS.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a formal full EIA and from ICPE (Installation Classée pour la Protection de l'Environnement) authorization, as the EMI office and cloud-hosting structure creates no industrial site meeting Code de l'Environnement Article R.511-9 thresholds; only a light environmental registration applies for backup diesel generators below 350 kW (rubric 2910) or for IT equipment WEEE waste streams.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC or process emissions; domestic sewage only, discharged to the municipal sewer under applicable local sanitation bylaws; Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment (WEEE) must be handled via certified DEEE collection channels per Environment Code Articles R.541-178 et seq.; annual greenhouse-gas emissions inventory (Bilan GES) mandatory for more than 500 employees per Energy Code Article L.229-25; cooling and backup-power installations, if any, must respect noise limits of 70 dB(A) at property boundary and fluorinated-gas (F-gases) regulated under Regulation (EU) 517/2014.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety compliance certificate for the office under the ERP (Établissement Recevant du Public) regime issued by the Commission de Sécurité before public occupancy; structural load clearance for server racks and vaults delivered by an approved contrôleur technique; electrical conformity attestation (attestation de conformité) for the premises; evacuation plans and fire extinguisher/sprinkler certification; occupational hazard assessment (DUERP) filed with DREETS and registration in the company's social documentation; mandatory annual preventive-medicine visit and workplace conditions clearance under Code du Travail Articles L.4121-1 to L.4121-5.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP); online portal: impots.gouv.fr; corporate formalities portal: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (guichet unique)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the SARL established in France, incorporation via the ONE-INPI guichet unique automatically assigns SIREN/SIRET (INSEE) and the intra-Community VAT ID (FR + 2-digit key + 9-digit SIREN), kept in the DGFiP taxpayer account. The legal representative of the newly formed SARL files the first DGFiP registration (liquidation initiale) and must complete the 'Déclaration de création d'entreprise' with a functional bank account; the VAT identification is issued electronically in the EDI dossier. Foreign-owned SARLs need a lawful French address for the registered office, a managing director with a valid domicile, and the publication of a 'statuts' registration in the Journal d'Annonces Légales; the DGFiP will issue the SIRET and the FR TVA intracommunautaire number within about 1 to 4 weeks. For pre-incorporation VAT purposes, the manager may use the provisional registration service of a chartered accountant (expert-comptable) through the 'service des impots des entreprises non établies' (SI NE) at Noisy-le-Grand.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; French-resident SARL is subject to corporate income tax ('Impôt sur les Sociétés', IS) on worldwide profits (CGI Art. 209 I); territorial scope is expanded for resident companies, unlike branch taxation for non-residents. New/existing eligible SMEs may apply the 15% reduced IS rate on the first €42,500 of profits, provided turnover < €10M; financial services of an EMI are French-source and therefore fully within French taxing domain. Tax classification excludes CFC treatment within the EU for a French tax-resident subsidiary? Actually the EMI is a French resident — out of scope.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: SARL family option (CGI Art. 239. AA) allows a 'SARL de famille' to elect transparent partnership taxation, but a licensed EMI can only qualify if all shareholders (joint holders) are family members; this election is available at the DGFiP within the first 3 months of the tax year and is a dual risk. Group tax consolidation ('intégration fiscale', CGI Art. 223 A) may be elected by a French parent with 95% voting rights. Hybrid mismatch disallowed: France applies ATAD 1 & 2 (CGI Art. 212 bis) denying deductions for payments that derive from double non-taxation arrangements, including hybrid financial instruments and reverse hybrid mismatches; no check-the-box equivalent exists. For VAT, the 'assujetti unique' group option (CGI Art. 256 C IV) allows the EMI to join a VAT group for simplified filing of exempt financial services.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Legal registration is mandatory for any taxable person established in France (CGI Art. 286), so there is no economic threshold; a micro-business 'franchise en base de TVA' (exemption) applies below EUR 91,900 (2025) for goods sales, but this measure is not accessible to financial services carrying the exemption of Art. 261 C. For non-established EU businesses supplying electronic, telecom, broadcasting services, France applies the EU EUR 10,000 annual EU-distance-sale threshold that does not relieve from registration, because France allows the customer-location rule; the EMI's VAT identification is mandatory ab initio due to the exempt financial services it renders.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory national e-invoicing for domestic B2B transactions is phased: from 1 Sept 2026 all large and mid-sized companies must issue and receive e-invoices; from 1 Sept 2027 SMEs must issue and 1 Sept 2028 for all remaining companies to receive. Invoices must be transmitted through the state public portal (Portail Public de Facturation, PPF) or a registered 'Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire' (PDP) in structured formats (Factur-X, UBL, CII), with systematic 'e-reporting' of transaction data to DGFiP. There is no real-time per-invoice fiscal clearance in standard sectors; however, the DGFiP receives transaction datasets via the PDP network at high frequency within 30 business days after the reporting period and carries out machine audits of the FEC (Fichier des écritures comptables) requirement. The EMI is also subject to the separate 3DS/PSD2 reporting and is captured by the DGFiP for CA3/VAT emissions regardless of the exempt status.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods physically exported from the EU, the French exporter applies 0% on the invoice (exonération, Art. 262 I CGI), with covert right to deduct input VAT. Services: as an EMI, the issuance of virtual IBANs and digital wallet reserve management are intra-Community and export services covered by the Article 261 C exemption (exempt without recovery) if the customer is outside France; the French place-of-supply rules (Art. 259 A. 259 B) bring B2B services to the customer's establishment and do not produce a zero-rating entitlement. For pure export of digital payment software/data hosting to a non-EU business, the services remain exempt and input VAT is blocked. The 0% scheme for exports is therefore limited to tangible goods; for an EMI without goods, zero-rating is only available for exported software licensing where software qualifies as assimilated goods — not relevant for an electronic money institution.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/DAU lodged in DELTA-X7 to customs, with MRN reference)
Transport document (Bill of Lading, CMR consignment note or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from the EU)
Inward Remittance Certificate (currency movement record on French exchange balance)
Commercial invoice and exporting sales contract
Loading and inspection certificates (if applicable by chamber of commerce)

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF), operating with the Direction Générale du Trésor for foreign-investment screening and with the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) as the prudential and AML/CFT supervisor for e-money institutions; the European Central Bank governs euro-area monetary operations and T2/TARGET settlement finality.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full de jure and de facto convertibility. France is a euro-area Member State applying Articles 63–66 TFEU on free movement of capital and Code monétaire et financier (CMF) Book I, Title V on financial relations with foreign states. There is no exchange-control authorization regime, no dual-rate system, no current-account versus capital-account convertibility distinction, and no profit-remittance convertibility hurdle. The only frictions are non-FX: EU autonomous sanctions screening, AML/CFT obligations (CMF Book V), ACPR safeguarding and segregation requirements for e-money float (CMF Article L526-14 et seq.), and inbound foreign-direct-investment authorization for non-EU investors under Décret n°2019-1590/Regulation (EU) 2019/452 where sensitive sectors are touched. Dividend remittances to non-resident shareholders are subject solely to French withholding tax rules (12.8% PFU for individuals, 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying EU/EEA corporate shareholders, treaty relief otherwise) — a tax matter, not a convertibility restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. French law imposes no statutory surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. A French EMI or SARL may freely hold, transfer and convert export proceeds invoiced in EUR or foreign currency. Residual obligations are statistical and bank-mediated: resident credit institutions and payment/e-money institutions must report cross-border direct investment, deposit, loan, securities and money-market flows to Banque de France under CMF Article R152-1 and the ECB balance-of-payments reporting framework (Regulation (EC) No 184/2005), using EU Bop6 classification codes. No FX conversion or repatriation requirement attaches to these reports.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Compte Bloqué) & Operational Account (Compte de Fonctionnement)
Capital Escrow Account (Compte Bloqué), Operational Account (Compte de Fonctionnement) & Client-Funds Safeguarding Account (Compte de Cantonnement)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Compte Bloqué) & Operational Account (Compte de Fonctionnement)
Operational Account (Compte de Fonctionnement) & Safeguarding Escrow Account
Operational Account only; limited appetite for EMI escrow or safeguarding structures

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium-High with strict legal constraints. A French-licensed EMI may lawfully use EEA-regulated fintech and EMI correspondents as technical issuers of virtual IBANs or custodians of segregated safeguarding accounts under Directive (EU) 2015/2366 (PSD2) and Directive 2009/110/EC (EMD2), but the French SARL must remain the supervised entity responsible for end-client due diligence and safeguarding. Offshore digital EMIs established in the UK post-Brexit no longer benefit from EU passporting and would require a separate ACPR licence or French agent registration to onboard French clients, making them unviable as primary treasury counterparties. EEA EMIs (e.g., Lithuanian or German licensed e-money/payment institutions) can be used as sub-processors or white-label IBAN platforms only where an ACPR-approved outsourcing agreement and clear contractual liability cascade exist. In practice, the French EMI should hold its master operational and safeguarding accounts with a Tier-1 French or EU credit institution and use foreign digital EMIs solely for ancillary IBAN distribution, not for reserve custody.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory in practice for a High_Risk_Special_License EMI: the beneficial owner(s), the gérant(s) of the SARL, and the designated AML/CFT compliance officer must attend an in-person onboarding interview at the bank's French head office or regional corporate centre. The legal basis is CMF Article L561-5 (identification before establishing a business relationship) and ACPR guidance on enhanced due diligence; remote video verification permitted by CMF Article L561-5-1 for digital identity capture is not sufficient alone for an e-money institution because banks impose counterparty risk committees for EMI sponsors. A remote-only onboarding route is not a viable or durable pathway for the described virtual IBAN/digital wallet reserve model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual IBAN white-labelling or resale of payment infrastructure to unregulated e-money/digital-wallet brands
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Certified ACPR e-money institution licence (agrément) with scope statement; (ii) ACPR-approved internal control programme and compliance officer CV; (iii) detailed white-label agreements with contractual AML responsibility allocation; (iv) safeguarding account segregation attestation from the custodian bank; (v) eKYC vendor audit and identity assurance certification under PSD2; (vi) transaction-monitoring system configuration, threshold calibration and alert-to-case conversion statistics; (vii) sanctions/PEP screening logs and matching policy; (viii) 24-month audited financial statements and capital certificate evidencing €350,000 initial capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transnational ownership layers with opaque beneficial ownership and borderline 25% UBO thresholds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) RCS Kbis extract and full constitutional file of the SARL; (ii) notarized beneficial-ownership declaration under CMF Article L561-2-1; (iii) group organigram showing legal and economic ownership percentages; (iv) LEI codes for all intermediate vehicles; (v) passport copies and proof of address for all UBOs; (vi) source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence for capital contributors; (vii) board resolution confirming no deliberate splitting of shareholding to fall below the 25% declaration threshold.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction velocity and cross-border payment flows inconsistent with the stated reserve-management business model, including exposure to sanctioned jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Approved business plan with transaction-volume stress tests and liquidity forecasts; (ii) daily safeguarding ledger reconciliation trial balance; (iii) AML/CFT policy document prepared in line with ACPR Position 2018-01; (iv) geopolitical sanctions risk matrix mapping EU/OFAC/OFSI sanctions lists; (v) merchant and partner due-diligence files; (vi) external auditor's opinion on internal control system; (vii) TRACFIN suspicious-transaction declarations or documented non-suspicion rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound funding of virtual IBANs from cryptocurrency exchanges or unregulated digital-asset platforms
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Formal policy on crypto-related credit transfers and so-called digital-asset service provider exposure; (ii) EU MiCA transitional registration or AMF-registered DASP documentation of any linked virtual-asset entities; (iii) documented source-of-funds escalation cases; (iv) monitoring rules flagging crypto-origin deposits above defined thresholds; (v) evidence of limit setting and cooling periods on crypto-linked IBANs; (vi) TRACFIN interaction record; (vii) ACPR/AMF guidance compliance self-assessment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete FATCA/CRS documentation for non-resident shareholders and cross-border beneficiaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) FATCA declarations (Form W-8BEN/W-8BEN-E or W-9) with valid US TINs or documented exemption codes; (ii) CRS self-certifications for each non-resident shareholder; (iii) Tax Residency Certificates from the shareholder's jurisdiction; (iv) annual CRS exchange filing record to DGFiP; (v) shareholder register with updated documentation trails; (vi) legal tax-opinion confirming no French PE or corporate-residence trigger for non-resident shareholders; (vii) AEOI compliance attestation from the appointed reporting intermediary.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (i) Equity subscription proceeds must arrive in EUR via SWIFT MT103/MT202 to the French SARL's euro operating account, with remittance information referencing the corporate identifier 'FR__FR__FR_SARL' and clearly marked in field 70 as 'Equity subscription – share capital contribution – non-distributable reserve' corresponding to ECB/Banque de France Bop6 direct investment equity category (FDI instrument type A.5); (ii) EUR 350,000 minimum initial capital under EMD2 Article 4(1)/CMF Article L526-10 must be confirmed by the receiving bank and evidenced in the statutory auditor's capital attestation to the ACPR; (iii) the payment must carry a valid UETR (Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference) under ISO 20022, and the originator must be disclosed with full name, address and account number to satisfy CMF R561-1 and the FATF travel rule; (iv) any non-resident shareholder funding must be accompanied by FATCA/CRS self-certification and source-of-funds evidence; (v) for sensitive-sector FDI, a prior authorization from the French Treasury may be required where the investor is non-EU and the activity triggers Décret n°2019-1590 screening; (vi) no French exchange-control approval is needed, but the bank will block or reject any transfer that cannot be tied to a clear commercial or institutional purpose.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) under the EPC Rulebooks for intra-SEPA payments in ISO 20022 XML (pain.001.001.03 / pacs.008.001.02); (ii) TARGET2 / T2 real-time gross settlement via Banque de France central liquidity management for urgent euro disbursements; (iii) SWIFT MT103/MT202 for non-SEPA or correspondent-bank cross-border trade settlements, with field 70 remittance information limited to valid trade or treasury purpose descriptions and full originator/beneficiary transparency under the travel rule; (iv) commercial letters of credit issued through SWIFT MT700, with MT798 negotiation and MT754 advices where applicable; (v) SEPA Direct Debit (Core/B2B) for collections, each mandate carrying a Unique Mandate Reference; (vi) virtual IBAN payouts are technically executed under the sponsoring credit institution's IBAN range, with settlement finality occurring on the partner bank's T2 commercial bank account, thereby requiring the French EMI to maintain pre-funding liquidity on its T1 bank accounts; (vii) each outbound transfer must pass sanctions screening, AML monitoring and, where applicable, French balance-of-payments statistical reporting; intra-group treasury sweeps between the safeguarding accounts and operational account require full reconciliation and cannot be used to commingle client funds with corporate funds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright vanilla FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) with an EEA-licensed counterparty bank under ISDA or FXC documentation, used only to hedge reserve-currency timing mismatches arising from multi-currency virtual IBAN issuance

FX swaps and cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) executed for liquidity management and asset-liability matching of the safeguarding portfolio, subject to ACPR prudent-period separation and board-approved treasury policy

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted only for currencies with genuine non-convertibility or settlement restrictions where physical delivery is legally impossible, with counterparties limited to European and international banks holding full banking licences and subject to Basel III counterparty credit-risk capital treatment

OTC and exchange-traded FX options where commercially justified for hedging known multi-currency exposures, although speculative option strategies are prohibited by the EMI's internal treasury mandate and would breach the safeguarding restrictions of CMF Article L526-14

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CIRS) solely to convert fixed or floating EUR reserve yields into matching foreign-currency liabilities on the virtual IBAN float, provided the derivative is fully collateralised and within the ACPR large-exposure framework

stage_5.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For SARL: appointment of statutory auditor mandatory if exceeds two of three thresholds: total balance sheet €4,000,000, net turnover €8,000,000, 50 employees (Art. L232-16 Code de commerce). Independent audit is also imposed by ACPR/EMI licensing conditions on all electronic money institutions regardless of size.
stage_5.governing_accounting_framework: Individual annual accounts under French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général, ANC Règlement No. 2014-03); IFRS as adopted in the EU is permitted for consolidated financial statements when applicable; EMI prudential reporting uses accounting figures reconciled to French GAAP/EMIR regulatory formats.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax rate for financial years opened on or after 1 January 2023; an additional 3.3% social surcharge applies to large taxpayers with turnover above €7,630,000 and current tax liability exceeding €63,000, yielding an all-in headline peak of 25.825%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on the first €42,500 of taxable income for SME companies with annual turnover net of VAT not exceeding €10,000,000; tax holiday for young innovative enterprises (JEI) granting full exemption on the first profitable financial year up to €100,000 and a 50% exemption on the second profitable year; R&D tax credit (CIR) and collaboration tax credit (CII) reduce effective incidence; the 3.3% social surcharge is not due by entities below the relevant turnover and tax-threshold net.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (liassez fiscale 2050 series) filed exclusively by electronic transmission through impots.gouv.fr / EDI-TDFC (Échange de Données Informatisé) or via an approved teleprocedure.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal years ending on 31 December, the annual return must be filed by the first business day following 1 May of the next year; for off-calendar fiscal years, it must be filed within 60 days after the fiscal year end. Certain filers using EDI receive a one-month extension for the balance sheet annexes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SIREN, SIRET, corporate name, legal form (SARL), address, ACPR EMI licence number, activity code (ISIC 6619) and fiscal year opening and closing dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities with a French permanent establishment must ensure the French branch registration number is disclosed and appoint a French fiscal representative; for a resident SARL owned by foreign shareholders, state the parent company's name and country of residence in the identification box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2, Type of Company and Tax Regime
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicated tax status options: normal IS regime, integrated group member, reduced-rate small business option, or parent-subsidiary option; declaration codes specific to electronically created euro cash units.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Check 'permanent establishment' or 'autonomous entity' option as applicable; a foreign legal entity that merely holds shares in the SARL need not complete this line, but should attach a list of direct shareholders and controlled entities for transparency.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross taxable turnover excluding collected VAT, comprising digital wallet service fees, SEPA credit transfer commissions, virtual IBAN issuance fees, interchange and platform administration charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only income attributable to the French operation or source in France; for a foreign-parent-owned EMI, include intercompany management charges only if evidenced by arm's-length contracts and invoices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net profit or loss before current-year corporate tax; reconcile with certified financial statements; include accrued reserve interest and revaluation of e-money float assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident branches must adjust accounting profit to the taxable territorial basis and exclude expenses not incurred for the French branch; head-office cost allocations must comply with a signed cost-sharing agreement and the DGFiP's documentary requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit after applying loss carryforwards and statutory deductions; calculate at 15% reduced rate or 25% standard rate as applicable; add back fines, excessive director fees, or costs unrelated to French-source activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If treaty protection applies and the non-resident pays tax exclusively abroad, still file the French return if in the non-cooperative jurisdictions list or if the DGFiP has extended the territorial string; otherwise submit a formal non-resident exemption request and obtain a decision before zero filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing imposes a 10% penalty of the corporate income tax due (or 5% if filed within 30 days after deadline), plus monthly late interest at 0.20% per month on unpaid tax; a fixed penalty of €100 per omitted form or annex may be added. Intentional non-filing or fraudulent filing may escalate to a 40% or 80% sanction and criminal penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2571 (quarterly corporation tax instalments), transmitted electronically through the same EDI or impots.gouv.fr portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Instalments are due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December of the current financial year; if a statutory date falls on a non-business day, the due date shifts to the next business day. A balance top-up is filed with the annual return under 2065-SD.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicate the amount of the estimated corporate income tax for the current year, based on the preceding year's final assessment adjusted for expected changes in profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a French permanent establishment of a non-resident, the instalment base is limited to profits attributable to the French branch and subject to French IS; foreign losses are not deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the 15% SME reduced-rate tax attributable to the first €42,500 of taxable income; the remaining profits are charged at 25%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities are eligible for the 15% reduced rate only if they satisfy the SME turnover and ownership tests under French domestic law; the French branch must itself carry on activity and meet the relevant headcount and turnover thresholds.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct instalments already paid in the preceding quarters to avoid double payment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Keep evidence of foreign payment and any DTA equalisation; if a treaty credit relieves French tax, complete the relevant remission claim form before the final balance date.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to pay instalments gives rise to an automatic 5% penalty on the unpaid amount plus monthly interest at 0.20%; repeated defaults may trigger a formal IRS seizure (avis à tiers détenteur) and escalation to the 40%/80% fraud penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% statutory withholding tax on dividend distributions by French-resident companies to non-resident shareholders, unless reduced by an applicable tax treaty or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (which grants a 0% rate where the parent company holds at least 10% of the French subsidiary's capital continuously for at least two years).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficiary must provide the French paying entity with a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the tax administration of its state of residence, accompanied by a completed French Form 5000 (and, where relevant, Form 5001). The forms must be received by the paying entity before the payment date in order to apply the reduced treaty/DTA rate; where EU directive relief is claimed, the beneficiary must evidence the qualifying 10% shareholding and satisfy the twelve-month holding requirement. If documentation is not furnished before payment, the withholding tax is withheld at the statutory rate and refund must be sought through the annual French non-resident credit procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: French statutory withholding rate on payments of patent and know-how royalties is 30% on gross income for non-residents, but treaty rates generally range from 0% to 15%, and the EU Interest & Royalties Directive can eliminate withholding on related-consumption payments between associated enterprises of EU Member States. Interest: domestic law exempts ordinary arm's-length interest paid to non-residents from French withholding tax; however, a 30% withholding tax can reappear for interest paid to shareholders in a cooperative jurisdiction, interest on excessive related-party debt, or interest in abusive arrangements, while the EU Directive and most DTAs further reduce or eliminate the charge.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Master File documentation is mandatory where the French entity has annual turnover net of VAT equal to or greater than €50,000,000, or where the multinational group to which the entity belongs has consolidated revenues above €750,000,000; the country-by-country report threshold also starts at €750,000,000. The DGFiP may, after a formal request, impose compulsory transfer pricing documentation on entities below these thresholds if they operate related-party transactions exceeding €400,000.
